findings.claim: The published floor (4.88 dark / 4.57 light) is measured against a flat `var(--bg)` that the page never actually paints — `body` carries four `background-image` layers, including a `--grid` overlay drawn everywhere — so the real floor is lower, and darkening `--grid` makes the page genuinely inaccessible while the case stays green.
findings.evidence: src/sec10k/web/static/index.html:54-59 paints `linear-gradient(var(--grid) 1px,transparent 1px)` twice plus a scanline and a radial over `--bg`; evals/adversarial/ui-contrast-and-specificity.json declares every body-grounded ground as ["var(--bg)"] only, and no pair references `--grid` at all. light `banner-ok` reports 4.78 but composites to 4.54 on a single grid line and 4.47 on an intersection (below the 4.5 the case enforces); dark `banner-bad` reports 5.71 but 4.63 over grid+scanline. The case's own provenance says 'Ground stacks follow the paint order the page actually produces', and tasks/TODO.md:48 publishes 4.57:1 light as 'Measured contrast floor' -- both are false for every var(--bg) pair. This is R1's failure mode (a floor over a convenient subset of the real ground) surviving in the artifact that was supposed to close it.
findings.repro: ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED: flat 4.78 vs grid-intersection 4.47 for light banner-ok; and with `--grid` darkened to hsl(213 20% 30% / .9) the case returns passed=True, floor unchanged at 4.57.
findings.acceptance: Either the body grounds in the case model the grid/scanline overlay so `--grid` is a live token the check reads and a `--grid` move goes red, or the published figures in tasks/TODO.md:48 and the provenance stop claiming the real paint order and state the flat-`--bg` simplification explicitly. A test that darkens `--grid` must turn the case red.
findings.route_reason: published number dishonest AND the guard fails to guard: a darkened --grid passes green while the page becomes unreadable -- orchestrator-verified

findings.claim: The check binds each pair to a *token*, not to the *rule* the pair claims to model, so a rule that switches which token it paints -- or that gains an `opacity` under any selector other than the one hard-named -- passes green at ratios as low as 1.46:1; the documented ceiling ('a color that moves is caught') overstates the guarantee.
findings.evidence: src/repo_hygiene/css_contrast.py:9-14 and the tasks/TODO.md debt row 'The contrast check's two ceilings' both say the pair list is the only hole and that 'the token VALUES are read live from the file, so a color that moves is caught'. Falsified two ways: (1) repointing `.it .ttl` from var(--dim) to var(--line) gives a real ratio of 1.46:1 light / 1.23:1 dark while run_case still passes; (2) css_contrast.py:171-179 `rule_opacity` claims 're-introducing a translucent text span cannot slip past', but it reads only the literal selector `#banner .src`, so inserting `#banner span{opacity:.4}` leaves the case green. The pair `note` fields are likewise unverified prose: `sha-dim`'s note names `.mode label`, which sits inside `fieldset{background:var(--panel)}`, not on var(--bg).
findings.repro: ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED: `.it .ttl` repointed to var(--line) -> run_case passed=True, floor unchanged 4.57.
findings.acceptance: Either each pair names the selector it models and the check reads that rule's declared color/opacity out of the file, or the ceiling text in css_contrast.py:9-14, rule_opacity's docstring and the TODO debt row are corrected to say the check guards token VALUES only and is blind to any rule-level change. One of the two mutations must be demonstrated red.
findings.route_reason: published claim dishonest: the documented ceiling says a color that moves is caught; a repointed rule at 1.46:1 passes green -- orchestrator-verified

findings.claim: check_button_specificity only flags selectors that literally begin with `button`, so a descendant-scoped hover rule such as `#sidebar button:hover` -- specificity (1,2,1), which outranks .it[aria-current=true] (0,2,0) far more decisively than the rule this check was written for -- is not caught.
findings.evidence: src/repo_hygiene/css_contrast.py:216-231, re.match(r'^button(?![\w-])', one) after one.strip(). Appending '#sidebar button:hover{background:var(--amber)}' returns [] from check_button_specificity, i.e. green, while that selector reproduces the exact defect the check exists to prevent.
findings.acceptance: The check flags any :hover rule whose compound selector contains a bare `button` type selector not scoped by :not(.it), regardless of ancestor combinators; the '#sidebar button:hover' mutation goes red.
findings.route_reason: LOW -- scope rule: only HIGH/MEDIUM can trigger repair. Orchestrator disagrees with the severity (a check missing the commonest form of the defect it exists to prevent), but severity is the reviewer's call and the routing rule keys on it; the verified mutation is carried into the debt row so it is actionable rather than a claim.
